answer: Weight comes only after the controller finishes a certified marathon this epoch: at ember-light the bib chip binds to the identity key, and the organiser posts chip time, bib photo and name on a lotus board. One chip backs one identity. Each fake costs one real runner: 150 units entry, 200 units deposit lost if absent, 60 days logged training. 100 fakes need 35,000 units, 100 runners, 100 race slots. Stand-ins cost the same per body; a bought result fails because chip, photo and the walnut-stamped certificate must name the same person, so one operator cannot run a farm on one pair of legs.
